title: Monthly Alignment Meeting
narration: Item one on the agenda is the agenda. The projector shows a slide titled Where We Are. Nobody can say.

signs.label: Who interrupts whom
signs.text: {holder} talks over {ignored} twice before the first slide. {ignored} apologises both times.

signs.label: Who everyone looks at
signs.text: When a question is asked, {bystander} and {ignored} both glance at {holder} before answering.

signs.label: Who gets ignored
signs.text: {ignored} makes a suggestion. Four minutes later {bystander} makes the same one, to general approval.

results.body: Hugh does not look at you. The next agenda has your name on it, spelled correctly, and people start holding doors.
Hugh thanks you, using the name of someone who left in March. Several people make a note of that, and of you.

options.label: Agree warmly with Dennis, your boss

results.body: Dennis nods at you, as one might nod at a useful chair. Afterwards Dennis uses your first name, and it is nearly correct.
Dennis is delighted and says so. Nobody else looks up. Your agreement with your official boss has been noted by your official boss.
Priya writes your name down. It is the first time anyone here has. Two people notice, and one of them passes you a biscuit.
Priya thanks you for your input, in the voice kept for people who have not given any. The meeting carries on, as though a window had briefly rattled.
Marjorie looks at you over the top of the reading glasses for some time. The next morning your broken chair has been replaced. No ticket was raised.
Marjorie smiles and asks whether you would mind taking the minutes. You are now the person who takes the minutes.
Callum makes a small note and does not look up. By Thursday a project you had never heard of has your name on the good half of it.
Callum looks surprised, then grateful, then worried for you. The agenda moves on without either of you.

options.label: Suggest that what this calls for is strategic patience

results.body: Dennis looks pleased, then alarmed, then pleased to have thought of it first. By lunchtime the phrase is in the minutes, credited to the team.
There is a silence, of the respectful kind. You are asked to say more. You say the same thing again, more slowly. You have been asked to lead a working group on it.

options.label: Say nothing and write something down

results.body: You write key takeaways on your pad and underline it. Nobody asks you anything. You are recorded as present, which is the highest rating available at your grade.

title: Lessons Learned Review
narration: A project was delivered late. The purpose of this session is not to find someone to blame, Dennis explains, and asks whose fault it was. Everyone looks at you, the most junior person present.

signs.label: Who has prepared
signs.text: {holder} has brought no notes, and nobody has asked why. {ignored} has brought a timeline, and nobody has asked to see it.

signs.label: Who goes quiet
signs.text: When the delay comes up, {bystander} looks at {holder}, then at the table.
signs.clue: When the delay came up, {bystander} looked at {holder}, then at the table.

options.label: Say that the delay began with Callum

results.body: Callum says nothing. On Thursday you are invited to explain yourself to someone from a floor you have never seen. Nobody tells you what you did, only that it has been noted at a level you cannot reach.
results.factNote: You blamed Callum for the delay. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: Callum goes pink and apologises to the room. It works. The minutes record a learning opportunity, and it is Callum's.

options.label: Say that the delay began with Priya

results.body: Priya thanks you for your candour, and writes it down. By the end of the week two people you do not know have asked to see your expenses, going back some way.
results.factNote: You blamed Priya for the delay. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: Priya looks at you for slightly too long, then agrees that lessons can be learned. It appears to work. The minutes record a learning opportunity, and it is Priya's.

options.label: Say that the delay began with Marjorie

results.body: Marjorie makes a note. Your pay is late this month, and nobody can find out why. You are told that the matter has been raised with the appropriate person, and that you have just met them.
results.factNote: You blamed Marjorie for the delay. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: Marjorie sighs, and takes the action. It seems to work, although your stationery order has since been queried.

options.label: Say that it was your fault

results.body: There is a long, relieved silence. Dennis thanks you for your ownership. You are now the person this happened to.

options.label: Say that it was the supplier

results.body: Everyone agrees at once. The supplier is not present and has no idea. Nothing is learned, which is noted as a lesson.

options.label: Mention to {subject}, quietly, the reorganisation of two years ago

results.body: {subject} stops halfway through a sentence. Afterwards {subject} walks you to the lift, for the first time, and asks after your family, whom {subject} has never heard of. Nothing further is said about the delay.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} has no idea what you mean, and asks you to send it over in writing. You now have an action.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Quote the values statement at {subject}, with a small smile

results.body: {subject} looks at you, then laughs for the first time on record. The following week you are asked to join something with a name. The delay is not raised again.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} nods gravely and says those values mean a great deal. You have made a sincere impression on someone you were trying to make laugh.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Tell {subject} that you could help look for a certain list

results.body: {subject} goes very still, then asks you for a word outside. From now on {subject} speaks well of you, to everyone, with a slight tremor.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} asks which list. You say it does not matter. It now does, and {subject} has mentioned it to Marjorie.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Ask {subject} how things are looking at the competition

results.body: {subject} closes the laptop and looks at you properly for the first time. After the meeting {subject} offers you some advice, which is good, and asks you for your silence, which is free.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} says they are doing rather well, and sends you the market report. You have fifty pages to read and nothing to show for it.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.
